   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, February 5, 2019

   CALL TO ORDER
   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Menchaca

  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. CEREMONIAL SWEARING IN OF OFFICER CARLOS OCEGUEDA

  B. CEREMONIAL SWEARING IN OF OFFICER CHRISTOPHER LEFAY

  C. CEREMONIAL SWEARING IN OF OFFICER CECILY RAMIREZ

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes. I
  will give you a 30 second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to me before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please state
  your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. MATERIAL DEMANDS

   This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. INVESTMENT REPORT

  This is a presentation of City investments for the month of December 2018.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of January 15, 2019.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of January 15, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  D. ORDINANCE NO. 650 REVISING THE COMPOSITION OF THE DESIGN
  REVIEW COMMISSION - ADOPTION

  Adoption of this Ordinance would increase the number of Design Review
  Commissioners from three to five and allow for greater flexibility in the
  appointment process related to professional skills specificity. Ordinance No.
  650 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote of the City Council at the
  January 15, 2019 City Council meeting.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  650 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of San Gabriel, California,
  Revising the Composition of the Design Review Commission.”

  E. ORDINANCE NO. 649 REAUTHORIZING AND READOPTING THE CITY’S
  PUBLIC, EDUCATIONAL, AND GOVERNMENTAL ACCESS SUPPORT FEE -
  ADOPTION

  This Ordinance authorizes state-franchised video service providers to pay the
  City a PEG fee of 1% of the video service provider’s gross revenue attributable

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 5, 2019  3
   to the City, which will be collected from its subscribers. The fee collected is to
  cover costs associated with the “Cable Scroll” on the public education channel.
  Ordinance No. 649 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote of the City
  Council at the January 15, 2019 City Council Meeting.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  649 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Reauthorizing and Readopting the City’s Public, Educational, and
  Governmental Access Support Fee.

  F. THEATER RENTAL FEE WAIVER REQUEST: AMERICAN CHINESE CULTURE
  ASSOCIATION

  The American Chinese Culture Association (ACCA) has approached the City of
  San Gabriel requesting a waiver of the theater rental fee for their free
  performance held February 2, 2019. The request is in line with the City’s existing
  guidelines for fee waivers. ACCA has agreed to pay all other theater rental costs,
  including labor and equipment fees. The fee waiver of $3,560 will be charged
  to the Rental Subsidy Account #152-3532.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve ACCA’s request to waive the
  theater rental fee of $3,560 for the rehearsal free admission community
  performance held on February 2, 2019.

  G. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH AECOM TO CONDUCT AN
  ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MARKET STUDY

  In May 2018, City Council directed staff to solicit bids for a comprehensive
  analysis and market study of the Mission District. The Community Development
  Department circulated a Request for Proposals (RFP 18-13) seeking a qualified
  consulting firm to conduct a study. AECOM met all criteria and addressed all
  points in the scope of work outlined in the RFP at a cost of $74,540. The total
  cost for the comprehensive economic analysis and market study shall not
  exceed $75,000 and shall be paid out of the Capital and Special Projects Budget
  cost center, #122-800-15-96-781.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 5, 2019  4
   Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the professional services agreement with AECOM to conduct a comprehensive
  economic analysis and market study for the Mission District.

  H. AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE A MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING FOR THE CITY TO PARTICIPATE IN THE 626 GOLDEN
  STREETS MISSION TO MISSION CICLOVIA WORKING GROUP WITH THE
  CITIES OF ALHAMBRA AND SOUTH PASADENA FOR AN OPEN STREETS
  EVENT TO BE HELD ON MAY 19, 2019.

  On May 19, 2019, the cities of San Gabriel, Alhambra, and South Pasadena will
  jointly host an open streets event called 626 Golden Streets Mission to Mission
  Ciclovia. Open streets events are festivals where streets are closed to
  automobile traffic so that cyclists and pedestrians can experience their
  community in a manner without automobiles present. The event will open the
  streets from the San Gabriel Mission to Mission/Meridian Goldline Station in
  South Pasadena. The City will be responsible for an in-kind match of $9,495,
  which is expected to be covered through staff time planning and holding the
  event. There is no other fiscal impact anticipated.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for the City to participate in the
  Mission to Mission Working Group.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PUBLIC MEETING TO ESTABLISH THE SAN GABRIEL TOURISM AND
  MARKETING IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT

  The San Gabriel Tourism and Marketing Improvement District (SGTMID) is a
  benefit assessment district proposed to create a revenue source to help fund
  marketing and sales promotion efforts for San Gabriel lodging businesses and
  thereby increase the transient occupancy tax for the City of San Gabriel. This
  approach has been used successfully in other destination areas throughout the
  state to improve tourism and drive additional room night sales to assessed
  lodging businesses. The proposed SGTMID includes all lodging businesses, with
  100 rooms or more, located within the boundaries of the City of San Gabriel.

  San Gabriel lodging business owners with 100 rooms or more decided to
  pursue formation of the SGTMID in order to create a revenue source devoted
  to marketing San Gabriel as a tourist, meeting and event destination. If

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 5, 2019  5
   established, the SGTMID would generate approximately $193,000 on an annual
  basis for promotion of travel and tourism specific to San Gabriel.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council open public testimony to allow
  members of the public to provide comments on the formation of the San
  Gabriel Tourism and Marketing Improvement District (SGTMID).

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 19-04 RELATING TO COUNCIL REORGANIZATION AND
  REPEALING RESOLUTION NO. 95-01

  Consolidation of elections pursuant to the California Voter Participation Rights
  Act necessitates a change to the date mandated in Resolution No. 95-01 for
  Council reorganization in election years as this timeline cannot be met under
  County election administration. For consistency, there is also a need to
  memorialize the timing for reorganization in non-election years.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-04 relating to
  Council reorganization and repealing Resolution No. 95-01.

  B. CITYWIDE PARKING DISCUSSION

  Parking is an ongoing topic and issue in the community. Chapters 72 and 153
  of the San Gabriel Municipal Code regulate parking in the City of San Gabriel.
  For the last several months, an interdepartmental group of staff members from
  Administration, Community Development, Finance, Fire, Police, and Public
  Works has been meeting to discuss current parking issues and to provide City
  Council with short-term and long-term solutions to consider.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council provide input on this discussion item
  and direct staff to bring back an agenda item with specific actions for a future
  date.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 5, 2019  6
  7. PUBLIC COMMENT

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 11. ADJOURNMENT

  The City Council will adjourn the meeting in memory of Mary Maloof, longtime
  resident of the City of San Gabriel.

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, February 19, 2019
  at 6:30 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
  Gabriel, California. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.
